content: 1. Apalutamide Interaction: Apalutamide, a strong inducer of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, can significantly reduce the plasma levels of drugs metabolized by this enzyme. This may lead to reduced therapeutic efficacy of these medications. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or substitute with alternative drugs when possible. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose of the affected drug as per prescribing information. 2. Atazanavir and Norethindrone Acetate: Atazanavir can decrease the effectiveness of norethindrone acetate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternative medications should be considered if available. 3. Belzutifan and Hormonal Contraceptives: Belzutifan, by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, can reduce the levels of norethindrone acetate, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Women of reproductive potential should be advised to use effective non-hormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 4. Carbamazepine Interaction: Carbamazepine decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during coadministration, and alternative or additional contraceptive methods should be used. 5. Cenobamate Interaction: Cenobamate reduces norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and the dose of CYP3A4 substrates may need to be increased. Close monitoring is required. 6. Clobazam Interaction: Clobazam, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during coadministration. 7. Dabrafenib Interaction: Dabrafenib decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 8. Elagolix Interaction: Elagolix, a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, decreases norethindrone acetate levels. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates during coadministration and consider increasing their dose if needed. 9. Enzalutamide Interaction: Enzalutamide reduces norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and alternative methods should be used. 10. Exenatide and Oral Contraceptives: Exenatide may impair the absorption of oral contraceptives by slowing gastric emptying. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide administration. 11. Fedratinib Interaction: Fedratinib increases norethindrone acetate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary and monitor closely. 12. Fexinidazole Interaction: Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects from CYP3A4 substrates. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 13. Fosphenytoin Interaction: Fosphenytoin decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 14. Idelalisib Interaction: Idelalisib, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, increases norethindrone acetate levels. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 15. Iloperidone Interaction: Iloperidone, a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, may increase plasma levels of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Monitor closely for potential toxicity. 16. Insulin and Norethindrone Acetate: Norethindrone acetate may antagonize the effects of insulin, impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 17. Istradefylline Interaction: Istradefylline increases CYP3A4 substrate levels at higher doses. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates during coadministration. 18. Ivosidenib Interaction: Ivosidenib decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. 19. Lenacapavir Interaction: Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels for up to nine months after the last dose, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 20. Liraglutide and Oral Contraceptives: Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of liraglutide. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 21. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor Interaction: Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 22. Maraviroc Interaction: Norethindrone acetate increases maraviroc levels, potentially increasing toxicity. Monitor closely. 23. Mavacamten Interaction: Mavacamten decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should use non-CYP450-affected contraceptive methods during and after coadministration. 24. Mifepristone Interaction: Mifepristone reduces norethindrone acetate effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Backup contraception is recommended. 25. Mitotane Interaction: Mitotane decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 26. Phenobarbital Interaction: Phenobarbital decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 27. Phenytoin Interaction: Phenytoin decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 28. Primidone Interaction: Primidone decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 29. Rifabutin Interaction: Rifabutin decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 30. Rifampin Interaction: Rifampin decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 31. Rifapentine Interaction: Rifapentine decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 32. Rucaparib Interaction: Rucaparib increases norethindrone acetate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates as clinically indicated. 33. Rufinamide Interaction: Rufinamide, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, decreases norethindrone acetate levels. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 34. Siltuximab Interaction: Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6. Caution is advised when coadministering with CYP substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 35. Stiripentol Interaction: Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, may alter the effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Dosage adjustments may be required. 36. Tazemetostat Interaction: Tazemetostat decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 37. Tecovirimat Interaction: Tecovirimat, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, decreases norethindrone acetate levels. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness. 38. Topiramate Interaction: Topiramate decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration. 39. Tucatinib Interaction: Tucatinib increases norethindrone acetate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 40. Adverse Effects of Hormonal Contraceptives: Hormonal contraceptives may cause side effects such as edema, weakness, anorexia, amenorrhea, breakthrough bleeding, changes in menstrual flow, spotting, deep vein thrombosis, and thrombophlebitis.
